item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 251154
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several hundred miles
west of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on
recently upgraded Tropical Storm Julio, located well southwest of
the southern tip of Baja California Peninsula.
The National Hurricane Center has issued the last advisory on the
remnants of Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
east of Johnston Island,

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the
trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical
depression could form during the latter part of the week or early
this weekend while the system drifts generally north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Julio are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Julio are issued under
WMO header WTPZ25 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Blake

...LALA SHOWING LITTLE CHANGE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...34.9N 176.7W
ABOUT 515 MI...825 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 460 MI...740 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 34.9 North, longitude 176.7 West.  Lala is
moving toward the west-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h), and a slow
west-northwestward to northwestward motion is expected for the next 
few days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, and 
Lala is forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone on Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 53
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026 
985 
WTPA42 PHFO 251444
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  53
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026

The satellite presentation of Lala remains about the same as it has 
been for the last couple of days.  The cyclone continues to have 
well-defined curved bands of shallow-to-moderate convection with 
coldest cloud tops of -60 to -65 deg C.  Upper-level outflow is 
strongest over the northern semicircle of the circulation.  Based 
on an earlier scatterometer overpass with little change in 
structure since that pass, the advisory intensity remains at 45 kt.
 
Latest center fixes show that the storm is moving slowly 
west-northwestward with a motion estimate of around 300/5 kt.  The 
primary steering feature at this time is a weak mid-tropospheric 
ridge to the northeast of Lala.  The global models indicate that 
the stronger higher-latitude southwesterly flow will continue to be 
well-removed from the cyclone for the next few days.  Therefore the 
system is likely to continue a slow forward motion for the next 
72 hours or so.  The official track forecast is similar or very 
slightly to the west of the one from the previous advisory.  This 
is close to the latest corrected consensus, HCCA, solution.
 
Lala is forecast to traverse SSTs of about 23-24 deg C through 
Thursday and remain within a relatively dry low- to mid-level air 
mass.  These conditions should lead to slow weakening and gradually
diminishing deep convection.  It is likely that the system's deep 
convection will have decreased to the point that Lala will become a 
post-tropical cyclone by around 60 hours, and this is reflected in 
the latest NHC forecast.

-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.3N 164.1W
ABOUT 360 MI...575 KM E OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the remnants of Moke were located near
latitude 16.3 North, longitude 164.1 West. The remnants are moving
toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h), and this motion is expected 
to continue today.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For additional information, please see High 
Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, under AWIPS 
header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at 
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Remnants of Moke Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 250852
TCDCP3
 
Remnants Of Moke Discussion Number  20
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
Based on recent proxy-visible satellite images, the ill-defined 
circulation of Moke does not appear to be closed. A lack of tightly 
curved cloud lines on the south side of the system suggests that 
Moke has likely opened up into a trough. In addition, the sporadic 
bursts of convection noted earlier today have collapsed during the 
past several hours. Since Moke no longer meets the criteria of a 
tropical cyclone, this will be the final NHC advisory on the system. 
There are still likely 25 to 30-kt winds occurring to the north of 
the trough axis. The remnants of Moke are expected to move generally 
westward while gradually weakening over the next day or so.

This is the final NHC advisory on the remnants of Moke. For 
additional information, please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the 
National Weather Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header 
FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
